name: Activity view by object type

name: App's own queries left out of activity

Both names are settings: QUERY_TAG (env, default 'access-explorer', access.py:93) is set on the app's connection (sf.py:35); STREAMLIT_APP (env, default ST_ACCESS_EXPLORER, read into APP_ST, access.py:94) is the app inside Snowflake. activity_sql and ACT_BASE drop QUERY_HISTORY rows with that tag, rows whose StreamlitName is that app, and the TBL_ACCESS_ tables SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT writes (access.py:1332-1338, 4440-4441); quotes and backslashes are escaped first (access.py:1309, quoted() at 4493). name: Grant path behind a use

name: Activity read window (incremental)
summary: Window = ACTIVITY_DAYS (60) back from now, cut at UTC midnight (TIMESTAMP_TZ literal, not the session time zone); rows of an earlier read are kept up to the day before its last day, and that day onwards is read again (ACCESS_HISTORY lags up to 3 hours). Same in SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT activity() (sql/1_setup.sql:788-796).

Names from the link are kept on one line with backslashes and quotes escaped (one_line, quoted, lit), so no name can start a statement of its own. See logic/page-sql.md.

name: Rule 1: Technical role granted to a user or group role
summary: Technical role granted to a user or group role. Why: Technical roles belong under functional roles only. Severity Medium (access.py:166).

name: Rule 10: Person can write to a sensitive object
summary: Person can write to a sensitive object. Why: Writes to sensitive data should come from the build or a service user. Severity Medium (access.py:167).

name: Rule 11: Sensitive object reachable through a group role
summary: Sensitive object reachable through a group role. Why: Group membership is managed outside Snowflake, so reviews miss it. Severity Low (access.py:167).

name: Rule 12: Admin role is a user's default role
summary: Admin role is a user's default role. Why: Every session starts with admin rights. Severity High (access.py:167).

name: Rule 13: Orphan role: no users and no parent roles
summary: Orphan role: no users and no parent roles. Why: Unused roles hide access that nobody reviews. Severity Low (access.py:167).

name: Rule 14: f'Chain deeper than {MAX_DEPTH_RULE} roles'
summary: f'Chain deeper than {MAX_DEPTH_RULE} roles'. Why: Long chains are hard to review and hide where access comes from. Severity Low (access.py:167).

name: Rule 15: Future grant in a schema that holds sensitive data
summary: Future grant in a schema that holds sensitive data. Why: New tables there are readable before anyone classifies them. Severity Medium (access.py:167).

name: Rule 16: f'Dormant user (no login for {DORMANT_DAYS} days) still holds roles'
summary: f'Dormant user (no login for {DORMANT_DAYS} days) still holds roles'. Why: Unused accounts are an easy way in. Severity Medium (access.py:168).

name: Rule 17: Read-only role can write
summary: Read-only role can write. Why: The role name or its use says read-only, but it can change data. Severity High (access.py:168).

name: Rule 18: Unusual privilege set
summary: Unusual privilege set. Why: The role holds more or fewer privileges than its capability (READ, WRITE, ...) stands for, so its name no longer tells what it can do. Severity Low (access.py:168).

name: Rule 19: EXECUTE TASK held by a person or consumer role
summary: EXECUTE TASK held by a person or consumer role. Why: Running tasks belongs to the build or a service user. Severity Medium (access.py:168).

name: Rule 2: Direct privilege on a functional role
summary: Direct privilege on a functional role. Why: Privileges sit on technical roles, so the role model stays reviewable. Severity Medium (access.py:166).

name: Rule 20: OPERATE on a task outside owner/build roles
summary: OPERATE on a task outside owner/build roles. Why: The task runs with its owner's privileges, so whoever can start or resume it borrows them. Severity High (access.py:168).

name: Rule 21: Warehouse MODIFY or OPERATE outside owner/build roles
summary: Warehouse MODIFY or OPERATE outside owner/build roles. Why: Resizing, suspending or resuming a warehouse changes cost and availability for everyone. Severity Medium (access.py:168).

name: Rule 22: Stream on sensitive table readable without the table
summary: Stream on sensitive table readable without the table. Why: A stream returns the table's changed rows, so it leaks data its reader cannot read in the table. Severity High (access.py:168).

name: Rule 23: CREATE privilege on a schema held by a read-only role
summary: CREATE privilege on a schema held by a read-only role. Why: A read-only role that can create objects can copy data or change the schema. Severity High (access.py:169).

name: Rule 24: Person changed data or a table's definition
summary: Medium. A person (in USER, not a service user) ran WRITE or DDL on a known object with a role that has no OWNERSHIP reach on it (data_use(role)[1][object] lacks "own"); one finding per user and object: statement counts, the most used role, last day. access.py:6204-6214

name: Rule 25: Service user used from an interactive client
summary: High. A service user (is_service) has activity rows whose CLIENT is in INTERACTIVE (Snowflake UI, SnowSQL, Snowflake CLI); one finding per service user: queries per client label, tables, last day. access.py:6199-6200,5192-5198

name: Rule 26: Admin role used to read or change data
summary: High. Activity rows whose ROLE_NAME is in ADMIN on a known object; one finding per user and admin role: objects read, objects changed (action not READ), first three names. access.py:6201-6202,5199-5203

name: Rule 27: First access to a table in the last 7 days
summary: Low. Per user and object: the first day on the object is within the last NEW_DAYS (7) days of the snapshot and the user had activity before cut - NEW_DAYS (not a new user); detail adds "sensitive" for tagged objects. access.py:6193,5179-5183

name: Rule 28: Unusual volume on a table
summary: Medium. Per user and object with at least 5 active days: the busiest day has >= SPIKE[1] (50) queries and more than SPIKE[0] (3) x the median day. access.py:6220-6227

name: Rule 29: Streamlit app shows its owner's sensitive data to people who cannot read it
summary: High. Per Streamlit app (kinds STREAMLIT) whose owner roles (OWNERSHIP) read sensitive objects, per role holding USAGE on the app: users reaching that role who cannot read some of those objects through their own roles (user_reads) -> one finding on the holder role: app, owner, sensitive objects, users. Fix: revoke the app's USAGE from the role. access.py:5354-5369, app_exposure access.py:5314-5327

name: Rule 3: READ held directly and through another role
summary: READ held directly and through another role. Why: The direct grant is redundant and survives when the other one is removed. Severity Low (access.py:166).

name: Rule 4: OWNER role held by a consumer
summary: OWNER role held by a consumer. Why: Owners can drop and re-grant objects; only the build identity should own. Severity High (access.py:166).

name: Rule 5: Admin role held by a person
summary: Admin role held by a person. Why: Admin roles bypass the role model; use them through break-glass only. Severity High (access.py:166).

name: Rule 6: Sensitive column without a masking policy
summary: Sensitive column without a masking policy. Why: Everyone who can read the object sees the value in clear. Severity Medium (access.py:166).

name: Rule 7: Dormant or disabled person can read sensitive data
summary: Dormant or disabled person can read sensitive data. Why: Unused access to sensitive data is pure risk. Severity High (access.py:166).

name: Rule 8: Disabled user still holds roles
summary: Disabled user still holds roles. Why: Re-enabling the user brings all access back at once. Severity Low (access.py:166).

name: Rule 9: Privilege granted to PUBLIC
summary: Privilege granted to PUBLIC. Why: Every user, present and future, gets it. Severity High (access.py:167).

name: Rules 17 and 23 walk only roles they can flag
summary: read_shares() counts per role the data objects reached, read only, written / owned, owned and schema CREATE grants; readonly_writes and rule23 skip a role neither the name nor the behaviour heuristic can flag before walking it

name: Server is the only SQL writer
summary: with_sql adds sql, roleDb, toDb to Compare / Request / Granted vs used changes; codegen.sqlOf only joins them

name: SESSIONS read only from a week before the first day
summary: activity_sql (and the same text in SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT) joins ACCOUNT_USAGE.SESSIONS created from 7 days before the first day read, not a year of sessions; a session open longer shows no client, so rule 25 may miss it

name: One ACCESS_HISTORY read for object use and activity
summary: history_sql scans ACCESS_HISTORY once (A0, from the earlier cut) for both; each part keeps its own cut; PART = USE / ACT rows split by history_rows (Direct mode) or one INSERT ALL in SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT history(). If the shared read fails, each step reads alone (one failing read fails only its step); not after a timeout (a read apart scans the same rows under the same limit)

name: One snapshot run at a time
summary: Insert the RUNNING row first, then only the earliest RUNNING run of the last hour goes on; others delete their row and return SKIPPED

name: Snapshot data tables keep no Time Travel
summary: TBL_ACCESS_ data tables are created with DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS = 0 and the RETENTION_* (may fail) statements set it on existing tables: each run deletes older runs' rows, so Time Travel would only store copies

name: Same snapshot run: nothing read again
summary: snapshot(old=cache.last): when the last OK RUN_ID equals the held data's and that data has the current shape (every table a list, no RUN_ID column, HOURS parsed), it is returned after the one TBL_ACCESS_RUN query; a new run reads every table again (test_server.test_same_run)

summary: STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_IN_SECONDS as a statement parameter, not ALTER SESSION (the same locally and inside Snowflake); none on the SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT CALL (a cut CALL would leave its run RUNNING). A timeout (error 000630, access.timed_out) raises TimeoutError '<step>: stopped after 5 min (STATEMENT_TIMEOUT=300); set STATEMENT_TIMEOUT=600 for 10 minutes', or says a lower warehouse / account limit stoppe
